source.author: ov
source.text: Et iam Dulichios portus Ithacamque Samonque Neritiasque domus, regnum fallacis Ulixis, praeter erant vecti: certatam lite deorum Ambraciam versique vident sub imagine saxum iudicis, Actiaco quae nunc ab Apolline nota est, vocalemque sua terram Dodonida quercu Chaoniosque sinus, ubi nati rege Molosso inpia subiectis fugere incendia pennis.
source.text_original: Et iam Dulichios portus Ithacamque Samonque / Neritiasque domus, regnum fallacis Ulixis, / praeter erant vecti: certatam lite deorum / Ambraciam versique vident sub imagine saxum / iudicis, Actiaco quae nunc ab Apolline nota est, / vocalemque sua terram Dodonida quercu / Chaoniosque sinus, ubi nati rege Molosso / inpia subiectis fugere incendia pennis.
source.text_english: And now they had sailed past the ports of Dulichium and Ithaca and Samos and the Neritian homes, the kingdom of wily Ulysses: they see Ambracia, long contested in the dispute of the gods, and the stone of the judge turned into a shape, which is now famous for Actian Apollo, and the land of Dodona, vocal with its own oak, and the Chaonian bays, where, with the Molossian king as their father, the impious flames fled on the wings beneath them.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Dodonida quercum Chaoniique vides famulam Iovis.
reuse.text_english: You see the Dodonaean oak, servant of Chaonian Jove.
